principles: Consent is layered: collection, storage, quotation, paraphrase, publication surface, attribution, future reuse, and withdrawal are separate permissions.
A contributor may be able to tell their own story without being authorized to reveal another person's private story.
Family permission is not a magic universal key; it is a risk-reduction and respect requirement whose adequacy depends on identifiability, conflict, and sensitivity.
Living contributors retain edit, contextualization, and withdrawal rights.
High-harm domains are private by default even with a willing contributor.

branches.trigger: Public institutional, clinical, scholarly, or family-facing source.
Hospice worker, nurse, physician, doula, chaplain, social worker, funeral director, coroner, first responder, or similar contributor.
Family member, friend, bereaved witness, caregiver, or survivor account.
First-person testimony from a person facing death.
Cultural, religious, Indigenous, family, or community-held practice.
required_artifacts: review by named community authority when possible

branches.trigger: Pediatric dying, suicide, overdose, custody, active legal process, graphic violence, war, disaster, or institutionally retaliatory context.

withdrawal_path: Receive request and verify relationship to contribution without demanding unnecessary detail.
Freeze the record and mark as withdrawn_pending_propagation.
Remove or mask public surfaces immediately if any exist.
Trace derived glossary entries, search aliases, summaries, and teaching surfaces.
Record a rollback event without retaining private reasons unless the contributor asks for a reason to be preserved.
Confirm completion to the contributor when contact is available.
